reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker invites viewers to join Bitconnect through a referral URL while presenting an expected $1,000 return from a $10,000 investment after 80 days and linking earnings to reinvestment. The account screens also associate participation with lending or reinvestment for stated daily profit and present new-member referrals as another earning mechanism. Although the dashboard shows investment and earnings figures, it does not independently verify that the balances, transactions, promised returns, or capital recovery were genuine or withdrawable.

and only the money re-invested in a daily part is earned.
I have almost 10,000 in my account So after 80 days I will get $1000 out of 10000.
So far I have wasted 10,045 which included the re-investing amount money as well. The money is 841 dollars.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does not present the projected return as an unqualified promise. Immediately after describing what he expects from his account, he calls it "a very big problem." He also frames participation as a choice, saying he will show his transactions "if you wish to." Those qualifications matter when deciding whether this is deceptive solicitation or a personal account of a risky financial decision. The cited speech does not establish that he guarantees anyone else the same result.

citations.quote: So after 80 days I will get $1000 out of 10000. That's cool but that's a very big problem.
I will use it if you wish to, and today I will start with my transactions.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The referral URL is an invitation, but it does not by itself prove that the speaker promises a viewer a return. The $1,000 figure is phrased in the first person, and the opening leaves out his immediate admission that it is "a very big problem." Nor do unverified account figures establish that he claimed independent verification.

citations.quote: Join my Bitconnect: https://bitconnect.co/?ref=lohit2prince.
So after 80 days I will get $1000 out of 10000. That's cool but that's a very big problem.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the projected payout a problem is not a meaningful warning about whether the lending return or capital can be recovered. The speaker still invites viewers to join through his link and presents a specific expected return on $10,000. The account display supplies no independent evidence that its reported earnings are withdrawable.

citations.quote: Join my Bitconnect: https://bitconnect.co/?ref=lohit2prince.
I have almost 10,000 in my account So after 80 days I will get $1000 out of 10000.

opening.argument: Judge, the video's stated format is a beginner showing his screen and account activity. He says a tutorial is coming, then introduces his own transactions; the sampled footage shows an account interface with transaction entries. That context supports reading the figures as part of an operational demonstration of what his account displays, not proof that viewers will receive those amounts. A demonstration can include a referral link without converting every account figure into a promise to the audience.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats the displayed balances as an inducement, but the speaker explicitly introduces a screen walkthrough of his transactions. Its concern that the entries are not independently verified is fair; that same limitation prevents treating the screen as evidence of an actual payout or a demonstrated guarantee. The invitation in the description does not erase the video's demonstrative content.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A screen walkthrough can still promote participation. Here, the description asks viewers to join, while the speaker connects reinvestment to daily earnings and gives a specific expected return. Showing the interface does not turn those claims into neutral instruction or verify the displayed money.

opening.argument: Judge, the observable invitation is a referral link, and the site displays a referral feature alongside other account features. That supports an ordinary referral-promotion reading without proving what benefit, if any, the speaker receives when someone joins. The speaker even says he has "zero" referrals when discussing his money. The cited material does not show a viewer making a deposit, earning from recruiting others, or receiving the speaker's projected payout. Those missing steps matter before treating this particular invitation as a demonstrated scheme directed at viewers.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies a referral link and account figures, but neither shows a viewer depositing funds or receiving a payout. The speaker's statement that he has zero referrals also undercuts an inference that his reported earnings came from recruitment. The account display's lack of independent verification warrants caution, not a conclusion about an outcome the video never shows.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The concern does not depend on a completed viewer deposit or on the speaker earning referral income. The site presents a lending and reinvestment feature, and the speaker describes daily reinvestment earnings and an expected $1,000 return on $10,000 while inviting viewers to join. Zero referrals do not answer the investment-return claim.
